text:
One possibility worth examining is that your interpretation of the fight is colored by your tendency to guard what matters, which is a quality that tends to show when you're at your best. This reflex to protect what you care about might make your version of the fight feel louder and more one-sided than it actually was. 

It may be that you're not hearing the other side because you're still in the midst of this reflex, where you're focused on defending your perspective. This can create a sense of imbalance, where your experience of the fight feels more extreme than it might be.

What does it mean to you when you feel like your perspective is being heard and understood in a relationship?
